title: The Universe and the Solar System: Our Cosmic Address

questions.question: The universe is estimated to be about how old?
questions.rationale: Cosmic microwave background and Hubble expansion measurements date the Big Bang to roughly 13.8 billion years ago; 4.6 billion is the solar system's age.

questions.question: Our solar system is located in which galaxy?
questions.rationale: The Sun is one of 100–400 billion stars of the Milky Way, in its Orion arm; Andromeda is the nearest large galaxy, 2.5 million light-years away.

questions.question: Which is the correct order of planets from the Sun?
options: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune
Mercury, Venus, Mars, Earth, Jupiter, Saturn, Neptune, Uranus
Earth, Venus, Mercury, Mars, Saturn, Jupiter, Uranus, Neptune
questions.rationale: Outward: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, then the asteroid belt, then Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.

questions.question: Which planet is the hottest in the solar system, and why?
options: Venus — a runaway CO₂ greenhouse effect
questions.rationale: Venus averages ~465 °C, hotter than Mercury, because its dense CO₂ atmosphere traps heat despite being farther from the Sun.

questions.question: The asteroid belt lies between:
questions.rationale: Rocky leftover planetesimals orbit mostly between Mars and Jupiter, marking the boundary of the terrestrial and giant planets.

questions.question: Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006 because it:
options: Is too small to be round
Has not cleared its orbital neighbourhood of debris
questions.rationale: The IAU requires a planet to orbit the Sun, be round, and clear its zone; Pluto shares its Kuiper-belt region with many bodies, failing the third test.

questions.question: One astronomical unit (AU) is approximately:
options: 149.6 million km — the mean Earth–Sun distance
questions.rationale: The AU is defined by Earth's average distance from the Sun; 384,400 km is the lunar distance, and 9.46 trillion km is a light-year.

questions.question: Saturn is famous for its rings and also for being:
options: The least dense planet — it would float in water
questions.rationale: Saturn's density (~0.69 g/cm³) is below water's, while Jupiter is the most massive and Venus the hottest.

questions.question: A 'shooting star' is technically a:
options: Meteor — a meteoroid burning in Earth's atmosphere
questions.rationale: Meteoroids are small debris; they become meteors as they burn in the atmosphere, and meteorites only if any part lands on the ground.

questions.question: Elements heavier than helium — including the iron in Earth's core — originated:
options: In the cores of earlier stars and supernova explosions
questions.rationale: The Big Bang made essentially hydrogen and helium; stellar fusion and supernovae forged the heavier elements that planets — and people — are built from.
